speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe exactly where the pain is located in your right groin and did you hear or feel a pop at the time of the collision?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any numbness or tingling in your right leg, and can you actively lift your right knee against gravity? REQUEST TEST: Pelvic_X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: No fractures identified in the pelvic ring or femoral neck, but alignment suggests posterior dislocation of the right hip.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the X-ray findings of posterior hip dislocation, I need to assess for associated injuries. Can you feel sensation in your right foot, and are you able to move your toes? REQUEST TEST: CT_Scan_Hip

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the CT scan is normal, we can rule out associated fractures. I need to check for nerve damage; please confirm if you have any weakness in extending your right knee or foot. REQUEST TEST: MRI_Hip

speaker: Doctor
text: Since imaging rules out fractures and soft tissue tears, the diagnosis is clear based on the initial X-ray. DIAGNOSIS READY: Posterior Hip Dislocation
